content:
If you've recently purchased a new Mac, like the just-released Mac mini or Mac Studio, you're probably looking to add a new external display to your setup.

Below are my recommendations, covering multiple product categories and price points, to give you more options.

Best External Displays for Mac

Apple Studio Display

When it comes to the best displays on the market, how can we not mention Apple's Studio Display? Although it's on the pricier side, it features Apple's signature outstanding design and comes equipped with a 27-inch 5K display.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: 600 nits
  • Color Support: Wide color gamut (P3), supports 1 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support
  • True Tone Technology: Automatically adjusts display color temperature to match ambient lighting
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports (up to 120Gb/s) and two USB-C ports (up to 10Gb/s)
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W

The Studio Display comes in multiple configurations with different prices, which we'll list one by one below. If you want to enjoy an iMac-like experience with your Mac, the Apple Studio Display is the only choice.

Standard glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Standard glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt-adjustable stand

Nano-texture glass with tilt- and height-adjustable stand

Apple Studio Display XDR

The Studio Display XDR was launched earlier this year and features several major upgrades over the standard Studio Display, including mini-LED display technology and a 120Hz refresh rate.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K Retina XDR display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with mini-LED backlighting and 2,304 local dimming zones
  • Brightness: Up to 1,000 nits SDR, 2,000 nits HDR peak brightness
  • Color Support: Wide color gamut P3 and Adobe RGB, supports 1 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: 120Hz with Adaptive Sync
  • Host Charging: Up to 140W

Of course, the price of these advantages is even higher than the standard Studio Display.

Samsung M9 Smart Monitor

The 32-inch Samsung M9 Smart Monitor is an attractive option for Mac users because it features a 4K OLED panel. My colleague Justin Kahn at 9to5Toys has already switched to this monitor, saying "using it with my Mac mini over the past few months has been a real pleasure."

  • Panel: 32-inch 4K OLED display (3840×2160 resolution) with anti-glare coating
  • Refresh Rate: 165Hz
  • Ports: DisplayPort, HDMI, USB-C, 2 USB-A
  • Built-in Camera: Yes, 4K
  • HDR Support: Yes (HDR10/HDR10+)

Although it doesn't offer 5K or 6K resolution like some models on this list, you'll enjoy the benefits of OLED, including deeper blacks and better color reproduction and contrast.

Buy the Samsung M9 OLED Smart Monitor:

LG UltraFine 6K

The LG UltraFine 6K represents LG's evolution in the high-end display market. It features a 32-inch panel with a resolution of 6144 x 3456 pixels and offers very rich port options. Here are the key specs:

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K Nano IPS Black display (6144×3456 resolution), 224 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color Support: 98% DCI-P3 and 99.5% Adobe RGB, supports 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • True Tone Technology: None; supports automatic brightness adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 5 ports, one DisplayPort 2.1, one HDMI 2.1, two downstream USB-C ports, and one upstream USB-C port
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt
  • Contrast Ratio: 2,000:1

Buy the LG UltraFine 6K:

Asus ProArt 5K Display

My colleague Jeff Benjamin tried this monitor in person, and it immediately caught my attention. The Asus ProArt (PA27JCV) 5K display offers the same 5K resolution as the Studio Display (5120×2880) and the same 27-inch size, but at half the price.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 500 certified
  • Color Support: 99% DCI-P3, 100% sRGB and 95% Adobe RGB, supports 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Adjustment: Ambient light and backlight sensors automatically adjust brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: One USB-C supporting DisplayPort Alt Mode, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, three USB-A, one downstream USB-C, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via USB-C

For more details, check out Jeff's full review. If you're looking for a 5K display to pair with your Mac, the Asus ProArt is hard to beat.

Buy the Asus ProArt 5K Display:

Asus ProArt 6K Display

If you're looking for a larger, higher-resolution model, Asus has options too. The new Asus ProArt 6K display (PA32QCV) is a 32-inch display with a native resolution of 6016 x 3384. Jeff called it "unbelievably good value" in his review.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 6K IPS display (6016×3384 resolution), 218 pixels per inch
  • Brightness: Typical 400 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color Support: 98% DCI-P3 and 100% sRGB, supports 1.07 billion colors (10-bit)
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz with Adaptive-Sync (48–60Hz)
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one HDMI 2.1, USB-C and USB-A hub, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 96W via Thunderbolt 4

The biggest selling point of the ASUS ProArt 6K display might be its price, which is significantly lower than some of the most popular 4K and 5K displays on the market.

Buy the ASUS ProArt 6K Display:

Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K (S80HF)

Samsung's ViewFinity S8 5K is another attractive option to pair with your new Mac, offering 5K resolution.

  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits
  • Color Support: 99% sRGB, supports 1.07 billion colors; HDR10
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Adjustment: Adaptive Picture automatically adjusts brightness based on ambient lighting
  • Ports: One USB-C port supporting 90W power delivery, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-A ports, one downstream USB-C port, Ethernet, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 90W via USB-C

Buy the Samsung ViewFinity S8 5K:

BenQ 27-inch 5K PD2730S Thunderbolt Display

This might be my current favorite choice. The BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K display comes with a range of Mac-friendly features, the most prominent being of course its crisp 5K resolution.

  • Display: 27-inch 5K IPS display (5120×2880 resolution), 218 pixels per inch, with Nano Matte coating
  • Brightness: Typical and peak 400 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 400 certified
  • Color Support: 100% sRGB, 100% Rec.709 and 98% P3, supports 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ports: One upstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one downstream Thunderbolt 4 port, one upstream USB-C port, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, one HDMI 2.1, one DisplayPort 1.4, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 90W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Hotkey Puck G3: Physical external controller with customizable buttons

Buy the BenQ PD2730S 27-inch 5K Display:

In-Depth Review: BenQ's 27-inch 5K Thunderbolt 4 Designer Display is a true Apple Studio Display competitor

BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Display

If you're looking for a 32-inch display to pair with your new Mac but want to keep the budget under $1,000, this is one of the most attractive options. However, the biggest downside is that you "only" get 4K resolution instead of 5K. But it has a comprehensive selection of ports, and the 32-inch panel retails for under $1,000.

  • Display: 31.5-inch 4K IPS Black display (3840×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch
  • Color Support: 98% P3, 100% sRGB and 100% Rec.709, supports 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: 60Hz
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Adjustment: No automatic ambient light color temperature adjustment
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 3 ports, two HDMI 2.0 ports, one DisplayPort 1.4, one downstream USB-C port, three USB-A ports, USB-B, and one headphone jack
  • Host Charging: Up to 85W via Thunderbolt 3

Buy the BenQ 32-inch 4K PD3225U Thunderbolt Display:

In-Depth Review: Should 32-inch 4K Mac displays have been ruled out from the start?

Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultrawide Display

If you want to pair an ultrawide display with your Mac, the Dell U4025QW is one of the best options on the market. It packs 5K resolution and a 120Hz refresh rate into a 40-inch display. It also offers rich port options, a matte screen, and other highlights.

  • Display: 39.7-inch curved 5K2K IPS Black display (5120×2160 resolution), 140 pixels per inch, 21:9 aspect ratio, 2500R curvature
  • Brightness: Typical 450 nits, HDR peak 600 nits; VESA DisplayHDR 600 certified
  • Color Support: 99% DCI-P3, 99% Display P3, 100% sRGB and 100% Rec.709, supports 1.07 billion colors
  • Refresh Rate: Up to 120Hz, supports VRR
  • Camera: None
  • Ambient Adjustment: Ambient light sensor automatically adjusts brightness and color temperature
  • Ports: Two Thunderbolt 4 ports, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 1.4, three USB-C ports, five USB-A ports, 2.5Gb Ethernet, and audio output
  • Host Charging: Up to 140W via Thunderbolt 4
  • Speakers: Two 9W speakers

Buy the Dell U4025QW 40-inch Ultrawide Display:

Samsung ViewFinity S65TC

For a more affordable entry into the ultrawide display market, the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC is an option, currently on promotion at nearly half price. Although it doesn't have all the features of other models, you still get a 34-inch ultrawide curved display and plenty of ports, including a Thunderbolt 4 port that supports power delivery.

  • Display: 34-inch ultrawide curved display, Ultra-WQHD resolution (3440×1440), 1000R curvature, offering an immersive viewing experience.
  • Brightness: Typical 350 nits.
  • Camera: None.
  • Ports: One Thunderbolt 4 port (providing up to 90W power delivery), one HDMI 2.0 port, one DisplayPort 1.2, three USB-A 3.0 ports, one RJ45 Ethernet port, and one 3.5mm headphone jack.

Buy the Samsung ViewFinity S65TC:

Conclusion

The above are just some of the best external display options to pair with a new Mac. They all feature excellent macOS integration, rich connectivity options, and unique sizes and designs.

Did you recently buy a new Mac? Which display are you using to pair with it? Feel free to let us know in the comments.
